title: Visual constraints upon avian behaviour
why: A Cardiff PhD thesis on how avian behaviour is constrained by eye design: eye size, retinal image brightness and retinal topographic analysis compared across bird species (stored abstract). The harvest listed it for four of the six Colluricincla queries ("Colluricincla vision", "Colluricincla spectral sensitivity opsin", "Colluricincla visual acuity" and "Colluricincla visual field"), and OpenAlex search appears to match words in the full text (my inference from its returning a thesis whose abstract names no species), so a grey shrikethrush may be named in its comparisons. Retinal topography gives peak cell density and from it acuity (acuity_cpd) and receptor spacing (interreceptor_deg). The screen tool lists it as the one candidate for those two traits (words: eye size, retina). Green open copy; not opened by this desk. The same thesis is already on the wanted list for Oriolus (harvest-37).

title: Evolution of color and vision of butterflies
why: Elymnias: a hit of the family review "Nymphalidae vision review" in this genus's harvest (the listing stores no abstract, so no keyword flagged it). The title says it covers the colour and vision of butterflies, and main's evidence file oa-12.jsonl logs from its abstract alone (authors Stavenga DG and Arikawa K) that nymphalid butterflies share a basic set of ultraviolet-, blue- and green-sensitive receptors, so the full text may tabulate the photoreceptor spectra of nymphalid species that include an Elymnias species (lambda_max_nm, spectral_range_nm). The same review is on the wanted lists of harvest-30 (for skippers) and harvest-35 (for Aporia and Hamadryas). Authors and journal are not shown in the harvest listing. Not opened. The desk's web pair for the spectral traits ("Elymnias spectral sensitivity" and "common palmfly spectral sensitivity") returned papers on other animals (an eel retina, a dung beetle, damselflies, Drosophila, a colour-changing spider) and five records shown without readable titles (PubMed Central PMC6028894, a Frontiers event abstract 10.3389/conf.fphys.2013.25.00029, a Springer article 10.1007/s00359-018-1267-z, a Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution article 10.3389/fevo.2016.00018 on four addresses and a scholars.lib.ntu.edu.tw record); none names an Elymnias pigment peak or spectral range, and none was opened.
get: bronze open access per OpenAlex (free to read on the publisher's page): https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1467803906000557
